item.title: A$K Lauren: How will huge IPOs influence my money?
item.description: Experts explain how huge initial public offerings including Anthropic, SpaceX and OpenAI, may already be making an impact on your funds.
item.dc:creator: Lauren Young
item.content:encoded: Q. How will huge initial public offerings (IPOs), including [USN:L6N45M16I TEXT:"Anthropic"], SpaceX and [USN:L6N45407M TEXT:"OpenAI"], influence my money? A. They already are making an impact — and you probably didn't even know it. I spoke to 11 experts, and nearly all of them noted that many investors own mutual funds or exchange-traded funds that hold an array of stocks and often track major market indexes, such as the S&P 500 or Nasdaq-100. “If you own broad index funds such as a marketwide US stock fund, you probably already own a little SpaceX," says Luke Delorme, director of financial planning and a financial adviser at Tableaux Wealth in Stockbridge, Massachusetts. And, he adds, you'll likely own some shares of Large Language Model (LLM) makers OpenAI and Anthropic when they eventually go public — without doing anything. SpaceX, the rocket and spacecraft manufacturer, priced [USN:L6N42G18Z TEXT:"the biggest-ever US initial public offering "]in June at $135 per share. It joined the Nasdaq-100 index within 15 trading days, the Russell indexes within about a week and the CRSP Total Market index (which Vanguard total-market funds track) within 5 days, Delorme notes. However, the amount you probably hold is small because SpaceX represents roughly 3% of the Nasdaq-100. Keep in mind that SpaceX is not yet in the S&P 500 because it requires a year of positive earnings, so it may not qualify until 2028, Delorme estimates. FOLLOW THE MONEY Investors who do not participate in IPOs still feel their impact . “Given the size of these trillion-dollar IPOs, these are real dollars that have to come from somewhere,” says Thomas Van Spankeren, chief investment officer at RISE Investments in Chicago. “There are opportunity costs.” Indeed, when an index adds a company, every fund tracking it has to purchase shares and to buy, it sells slices of everything else it holds. JPMorgan estimated SpaceX’s Nasdaq-100 entry [USN:L4N42Z001 TEXT:"would trigger roughly $4.3 billion in passive purchases"]. "Your portfolio could take a hit if you own that which others are selling in order to get in on the IPOs," says Andrew Herzog, an associate wealth adviser at The Watchman Group in Plano, Texas. Robert Persichitte, a certified public accountant and certified financial planner at Delagify in Arvada, Colorado, gives this phenomenon a name: crowding out. “Crowding out is when more investment options compete for investors’ funds," Persichitte explains. SHOULD YOU BUY THE IPO? Everyone I asked offered some version of "No." “Historically, when you have big IPOs, they are a sign of froth in industries, especially when they are all concentrated in one sector,” Van Spankeren says. But that does not stop investors from asking him about investing in IPOs. “I walked a lot of clients off the ledge with SpaceX," Van Spankeren adds. "They want to get in because friends are talking about it. I said ‘No.’ ” His advice? Let the excitement burn off first. SpaceX, after surging roughly 50% on its IPO, closed below its first-day trading price within a month. "Don’t chase things because they’re hot and attractive," Van Spankeren says. Jim Tewalt, a certified financial planner and president at Estate Planning Solutions in Glendale, Arizona, says that it is better to wait. On IPO day, he notes, media excitement is at its highest, the investment banks have marketed the offering heavily, the supply of shares is limited and retail investors rush in on fear of missing out. “As a result, many IPOs trade well above their offering price before fundamentals are fully understood," Tewalt says. "Give the new company a year to make sure they will make money.” His checklist includes watching what insiders do: “They know things we mere mortals do not.” Tewalt allows for the exception: Buying early can work when the company is already profitable, revenue growth is strong, the valuation is reasonable against peers and you genuinely understand the business. VALUATION MATTERS Experts say valuation is the real risk for IPO investors. "The initial excitement around these companies could also produce significant volatility, particularly if investors extrapolate extraordinary growth expectations into extraordinary valuations," says Kashif A. Ahmed, president of American Private Wealth in Bedford, Massachusetts. It is also important to note that these companies are going public after years of private growth, so ‘initial’ doesn’t necessarily mean 'early.' "If investors pay too much for growth that’s already priced in, even a great company can be a poor investment,” says Chip Lupo, an analyst with WalletHub. And the market is getting pickier. “We’re already seeing investors become more selective, with more than 40% of 2026 IPOs trading below their offering prices and several companies postponing listings because of valuation concerns,” Lupo notes. That selectivity is visible today. Anthropic's market debut is likely [USN:L4N4500J8 TEXT:"pushed into November"] to get third-quarter earnings results into its prospectus. OpenAI [USN:L6N45407M TEXT:"moved its IPO to 2027"]. Lupo’s bottom line: “I wouldn’t treat these IPOs as automatic investment opportunities. A company can be enormously valuable and still produce disappointing returns if investors pay too much for it.” It is another story, of course, if you're an employee of a company that's going public and receive equity. "Huge IPOs are not going to be too life-changing for most people unless you work for one of these companies and are getting a massive payout due to the IPO," says Michael Espinosa, a certified financial planner and president of TrueNorth Retirement Services in Salt Lake City, Utah. "Yes, they make a lot of news in the headlines. They may be historical in their size, but the biggest question is how will they actually affect your portfolio in 1 year, 5 years, or 20 years down the line?"

item.title: Mali separatists announce withdrawal from strategic northern town
item.description: A separatist movement in northern Mali announced on Tuesday it was carrying out "a controlled withdrawal" from a strategic town in the north, a symbolic boost to Mali's army and its Russian backers in their years-long fight against insurgents including al Qaeda-linked jihadists.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A separatist movement in northern Mali announced on Tuesday it was carrying out "a controlled withdrawal" from a strategic town in the north, a symbolic boost to Mali's army and its Russian backers in their years-long fight against insurgents including al Qaeda-linked jihadists. The Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) took control of Kidal town six months ago in [USN:L6N41903L TEXT:"nationwide attacks"] that also killed Mali's defence minister. It had joined forces in those attacks with the regional al Qaeda affiliate, Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin, known as JNIM, posing the biggest test yet to Mali's military leaders who seized power in coups in 2020 and 2021. The FLA's decision to leave Kidal came in response to airstrikes by Mali's military backed by Russian fighters, the Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) said in a statement. "The FLA specifies that this is a temporary operational measure, also intended to preserve its human and logistical capabilities intact. This methodical withdrawal from the area took place without any direct combat having yet pitted its forces against the enemy," the statement said. Mali has leaned on Russian security support for years, first from the Wagner mercenary group and then from the paramilitary group Africa Corps, which is made up of many former Wagner fighters. 'SYMBOLIC' BUT NOT DECISIVE VICTORY, ANALYST SAYS Earlier on Tuesday, Mali's military said it had launched large-scale air and ground operations in the region of Kidal. The goals of the operations included tracking down and neutralizing armed groups operating in the area, destroying their supply networks and restoring "lasting security" and free movement for people and goods, a Malian military statement said. Pro-government fighters, including Russian fighters, re-entered Kidal on Tuesday afternoon, a security source said. It was not clear on Tuesday how close Malian troops were to the town and whether they would immediately re-occupy it. Malian forces and Wagner fighters retook Kidal from insurgents in November 2023, the most concrete gain from their partnership — only to lose it during the attacks in April. "A successful recapture... affirms the military-led government's authority and boosts the army's morale, particularly after several high-profile setbacks both in the north and the central regions in recent weeks," said Beverly Ochieng, associate director of Control Risks. "This is also an opportunity for Africa Corps to reprise its role as the Malian government's security guarantor after appearing to lose significant ground, including in Kidal, since April." But the change of control in Kidal is still largely "symbolic" and not "decisive" in Mali's campaign against insurgent groups, Ochieng added. A source close to the FLA leadership told Reuters that the aerial operations by Malian and Russian forces began three days ago. The source played down the significance of the FLA's withdrawal, saying it was a measure to protect lives and equipment. "For us, war is not a race against the clock," the source said.

item.title: Record imports push US trade balance deep into the red in August
item.description: The US trade deficit widened more than expected in August as imports jumped to a record high against the backdrop of robust domestic demand, keeping trade on track to again subtract from economic growth in the third quarter.
item.dc:creator: Lucia Mutikani
item.content:encoded: The US trade deficit widened more than expected in August as imports jumped to a record high against the backdrop of robust domestic demand, keeping trade on track to again subtract from economic growth in the third quarter. The deterioration reported by the Commerce Department on Tuesday was despite President Donald Trump's aggressive tariffs on imports, which he has argued are meant to shrink the trade gap. The nation posted record goods trade deficits with at least three countries, including Mexico. Economists have long argued that the US did not have the capacity to produce enough goods to meet its consumption needs. "The administration's trade policies have largely been a failure, trade tariffs have done nothing to reduce America's reliance on the import of foreign-produced goods," said Christopher Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS. "The cost of American labor is simply too high to produce goods here cheap enough for consumers to even think about purchasing. Even if US manufacturers were willing, the factories could not be built here fast enough to produce the goods that consumers depend on." The trade shortfall increased 13.7% to $105.6 billion, the largest since March 2025, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis and Census Bureau said. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the deficit would be $102.0 billion. The trade deficit was at $79.8 billion when Trump was elected for a second term in November 2024. August's deterioration was flagged by data last week that showed an import-driven surge in the goods trade deficit. Domestic demand increased at its fastest pace in more than 3-1/2 years in the second quarter, reflecting robust consumer spending and business spending on equipment, mostly related to AI. The trend appears to have spilled over into the third quarter, with data last month showing strong [USN:L1N45M0L0 TEXT:"consumer spending"] in August as well as [USN:L1N45H0BU TEXT:"orders and shipments"] of nondefense capital goods, excluding aircraft. But businesses are relying on imports to meet demand. Imports increased 4.3% to an all-time high of $420.8 billion in August. Goods imports jumped 5.3% to $342.2 billion. They were boosted by a $9.1 billion increase in industrial supplies and materials, which include petroleum. Crude oil imports rose $3.3 billion while nonmonetary gold increased $3.1 billion. Nonmonetary gold is excluded in the calculation of gross domestic product. Capital goods imports soared $6.2 billion to a record high $146.4 billion, driven by semiconductors and other industrial machinery. But imports of computer accessories decreased $1.6 billion. TRADE SET TO WEIGH ON GDP GROWTH Exports rose 1.4% to $315.2 billion. Goods exports increased 2.2% to $205.7 billion, reflecting a $6.3 billion rise in industrial supplies and materials, mostly nonmonetary gold, crude oil and fuel oil. Capital goods exports rose $1.3 billion, lifted by semiconductors and computers. But exports of civilian aircraft fell $1.0 billion. Consumer goods exports dropped $2.2 billion, pulled down by a $2.4 billion decline in pharmaceutical preparations. The goods trade deficit increased 10.3% to $136.6 billion in August. When adjusted for inflation, it widened $8.7 billion, or 8.2%, to $114.7 billion. Trade has subtracted from GDP for three straight quarters, and economists estimate it could cut as much as 2.5 percentage points from GDP in the third quarter. Growth estimates for the July-September quarter are mostly above a 3.0% annualized rate, with consumer spending expected to offset the drag from imports. The economy grew at a 2.2% pace in the second quarter. Services imports rose less than $0.1 billion to $78.5 billion in August, amid a small gain in transport. Charges for the use of intellectual property fell as did travel. Exports of services also advanced by less than $0.1 billion to $109.5 billion. There were modest increases in charges for the use of intellectual property and other business services. Travel and financial services both declined. The nation had record goods trade shortfalls with Mexico, Vietnam and Malaysia. It maintained deficits with Taiwan, China, the European Union, South Korea, Canada and India among other trade partners. It, however, posted a record goods trade surplus with Belgium, while maintaining surpluses with the Netherlands, South and Central America, the United Kingdom, Hong Kong, Brazil, Australia and Saudi Arabia.

Astronomers have now found a world that rightly can be called a phoenix planet.Researchers said this exoplanet, as planets beyond our so

Alien 'phoenix planet' was born from the ashes of a dying star

An artist’s impression of a second-generation planet orbiting the white dwarf HS 0209+0832, the first such planet to be found orbiting a white dwarf, in this image released on October 5, 2026. Snehalata Sahu/University of Warwick/Handout via REUTERS

FAST

WASHINGTON, Oct 6 : In ancient mythology, the phoenix was a miraculous bird with a cyclical pattern of life and death, perishing in flames only to rise again from the ashes. Astronomers have now found a world that rightly can be called a phoenix planet. Researchers said this exoplanet, as planets beyond our solar system are called, appears to have been born from material expelled into space during the death throes of a star a bit bigger than the sun, and now orbits the highly compact stellar remnant that was left behind, called a white dwarf. It is classified as a second-generation planet, meaning it did not form from the swirling disk of material surrounding a newborn star, as Earth and other first-generation planets did, but rather from the leftovers of a doomed star. "This is the first example of a planet forming around a white dwarf," said Jamie Williams, a doctoral student in astrophysics at the University of Warwick in England and lead author of the study published this week in the journal Nature Astronomy.

The white dwarf is located about 250 light-years from Earth, near the constellation Cetus. A light-year is the distance light travels in a year, 5.9 trillion miles (9.5 trillion km). The planet is a gas giant perhaps slightly more massive than Jupiter, our solar system's largest planet. It orbits the white dwarf every 4.4 days at only 4 per cent the distance between Earth and the sun. It is so close that the blazingly hot white dwarf's extreme ultraviolet radiation is causing the planet's outer atmosphere to evaporate, with a portion then falling into the white dwarf. The planet's chemical pattern points to its second-generation origin. It is rich in niobium, copper and zinc, the type of elements that certain dying stars cast off when they expand in their death throes, indicating the planet formed from a disk of this expelled material that surrounded the stellar corpse. "In myths, a phoenix is born again from its own ashes. In the case of this planet, it is born again from the ashes of its dying host star, and therefore the planetary system is reborn. A second-generation planet is defined as one born after its host star dies — in this case after it has become a white dwarf," Williams said. The researchers used data from the orbiting Hubble, TESS and FUSE telescopes, and hope to use the James Webb Space Telescope to confirm their conclusions. A small number of potential second-generation planets previously have been identified orbiting pulsars, a rare type of neutron star, another type of stellar remnant. "White dwarfs are much more common than pulsars, and over 95 per cent of stars in the Milky Way will evolve to become a white dwarf. Therefore, there would be many more second-generation planets around white dwarfs than around pulsars," Williams said. While the newly discovered planet would be inhospitable for life, another second-generation planet potentially could be habitable. "If a gas giant formed around a white dwarf, then a rocky planet could form, too. White dwarfs cool predictably over time and as they get cooler, their cooling slows. So if a second-generation rocky planet formed close enough to the white dwarf then it could remain in the habitable zone for billions of years," Williams said. A RED DWARF AND A BROWN DWARF A second study published in the same journal describes another exotic celestial phenomenon roughly 300 to 500 light-years from Earth in the constellation Taurus. Researchers used the Zwicky Transient Facility at Palomar Observatory in California to discover a red dwarf star about 8 per cent of the mass of the sun in a tight orbit with a brown dwarf, an object too small to be a star and too big to be a planet. The brown dwarf is about 30 times the mass of Jupiter and a third of the mass of the star. These two companions orbit each other every 87 minutes at slightly more than half the distance between Earth and the moon, and the star's gravitational pull appears to be siphoning material from the brown dwarf. The researchers detected a hot spot on the star's surface where this material appears to be landing. "This is the first observed example of this phenomenon," said Aaron Householder, a Massachusetts Institute of Technology graduate student in astrophysics and lead author of the study. "The two objects are so close together that the entire orbit would fit inside the sun," Householder said.

Source: Reuters

item.title: 生活費危機、インフレ期待や貧困に長期的な影響与える＝ＩＭＦ
item.description:
Andrea Shalal
[ワシントン ６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は６日に公表した研究報告書で、食...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
生活費危機、インフレ期待や貧困に長期的な影響与える＝ＩＭＦ 10/6 22:27 配信

国際通貨基金（IMF）のロゴ。2024年11月撮影。REUTERS/Benoit Tessier

Andrea Shalal

[ワシントン ６日 ロイター] - 国際通貨基金（ＩＭＦ）は６日に公表した研究報告書で、食料とエネルギー価格の急上昇は今後より頻繁に起こる可能性が高いと述べ、こうした危機はインフレ期待を長期にわたって高め、貧困を悪化させ、経済の安定を脅かすと警告した。

各国政府が物価高騰を緩和するために用いてきた３０年間の戦略を検証するとともに、生活必需品に家計のより大きな割合を費やす貧困層が経験する高いインフレ率を考慮した新たな経済モデルを提示。新しいモデルでは、標準的なインフレ指標との間に０．８％ポイントの乖離が見られ、２０２１年から２４年にかけて、以前の試算よりも２３００万人多い人々が極度の貧困ラインを下回ったことが示唆された。

研究を共同で主導したＩＭＦのエコノミスト、キアラ・マッジ氏は「要するに、生活費危機は物価安定に影響を与え、生活水準を低下させ、格差を悪化させる」と述べた。今回の研究は来週に公表される「世界経済見通し」の一部となる。

ジョージタウン大学教授で元世界銀行エコノミストのシャンタヤナン・デバラジャン氏は６日に公開されたマッジ氏とのビデオ対談の中で、原油価格の高騰、高水準の債務、借入コストの上昇、そして今年のスーパーエルニーニョ現象による影響が複合的に作用し、発展途上国は深刻な危機に直面していると指摘。「これは低所得国全体の成長率が過去最低水準にある時期に起こっている」とし、「成長率は著しく鈍化している」と語った。

ロイター 関連ニュース コラム：食品値下げは広がるのか、日銀判断にも影響する分岐点に アングル：イラン戦争による肥料高騰、穀物生産減少で食料危機の恐れも コラム：米だけ「異世界」のＩＭＦ会合　イラン戦争無視で政権の苦境露呈 アングル：トランプ減税、ガソリン代高騰で効果台無し アングル：イラン紛争で湾岸諸国の食料安全保障に打撃、輸入依存度は80％以上 最終更新: 10/6(火) 22:27 ロイター

item.title: Australia's Green ruled out of first test v South Africa
item.description: DURBAN, Oct 6 : Australia all-rounder Cameron Green will miss the first test against South Africa after failing to recover from an abdominal strain, coach Andrew McDonald said on Tuesday.Green was hurt during the last one-day international against South Africa in Potchefstroom on Wednesday after being struck

Australia's Green ruled out of first test v South Africa

DURBAN, Oct 6 : Australia all-rounder Cameron Green will miss the first test against South Africa after failing to recover from an abdominal strain, coach Andrew McDonald said on Tuesday. Green was hurt during the last one-day international against South Africa in Potchefstroom on Wednesday after being struck in the stomach by a full toss from Corbin Bosch that left him writhing in pain. Two balls later, his attempted pull shot bounced off his gloves and he was not only caught but strained his muscles as he fell to the ground. "It's an odd one and had our medical team scrambling, so I'm not going to go down what the medical said around it, but there's not a hell of a lot of evidence in these injuries in cricket," McDonald told a press conference. "They said it's a stabilising muscle, so I think that's a better result than a rotational muscle."

Green remains in contention for the second test in Gqeberha and the third in Cape Town. "He's progressing pretty well, all things considered, on the back of the injury that he had to his abdominal. McDonald said. "He's still here for a reason, so there is some light at the end of the tunnel. It'll just be a matter of going through the rehab. "It's a bit of an unknown, but there's still optimism that he'll take part in the series at some stage," the coach added. BEGAN TOUR WITH SORE SHOULDER The 27-year-old started the tour of southern Africa with a sore shoulder which kept him out of the three ODIs against Zimbabwe, but he did play in the three ODIs versus South Africa. Green's absence will be a blow as he is considered one of the form players in the touring party, especially after he scored a first home test century when Australia suffered a shock loss to Bangladesh in Darwin in August. Cooper Connolly, 23, could be in line for a second test appearance after his February debut in Galle against Sri Lanka as Green's replacement although Australia will not be settling on their line-up until they better assess the pitch conditions, McDonald added.

Source: Reuters

Oct 6 : Saudi Arabia's ambassador to the US, Princess Reema Bandar Al-Saud, has joined All Women's Sports Network (AWSN) in an advisory role, as the media company seeks to expand coverage of women's sports in the Middle East and beyond. AWSN, a sports media platform co-founded by actor Whoopi Goldberg, said her appointment would support efforts to give female athletes greater international exposure. AWSN Chief Executive George Chung said Princess Reema's advocacy for women and girls in sport made the partnership a natural fit. "What she understands is that sports is a catalyst for change," Chung told Reuters. "We consider ourselves a global platform, not just to make sports from around the world more visible, but to make them available to women."

Chung said AWSN planned to stage its first sports festival in the Middle East in the first quarter of 2027. The events would combine games, training camps, entertainment and retail experiences, with the aim of giving local athletes access to international players and creating programming for the network. The company plans at least four festivals globally next year, including events in Saudi Arabia, the US and Britain, he said. The appointment comes as Saudi Arabia continues to invest in women's sports under its wider economic and social reform agenda Vision 2030. The Saudi Women's Premier League, launched in 2022, has sought to build a more professional structure for women's soccer in the kingdom. AWSN began airing the league's matches last year.  Saudi Arabia's sports investment has also drawn criticism from rights groups and others who say the country uses high-profile events to improve its international image. Chung said AWSN had faced no restrictions on its programming in the region and pointed to investment in women's teams, facilities and broadcasts as evidence of growing support for female athletes. AWSN has recorded steady growth in viewing of Saudi women's soccer, with audience levels rising between 20 per cent and 30 per cent per game, Chung said, while average viewing time increased by nearly 50 per cent over the season. He added that AWSN drew 1.5 million viewers in its first 10 days on Pakistan's Tamasha platform, a result he said underscored demand for women's sports beyond traditional Western markets.

item.title: Euro sube, ya que descenso de rendimiento de bonos franceses alivia preocupación sobre deuda
item.description: El euro subía el martes, en camino a su mayor alza en un mes, tras caer el día previo a su nivel más bajo en 17 meses, ya que el descenso del rendimiento de los bonos gubernamentales franceses atenuaba los temores sobre la tensión en los mercados de deuda de la zona euro.
item.dc:creator: Chuck Mikolajczak
item.content:encoded: El euro subía el martes, en camino a su mayor alza en un mes, tras caer el día previo a su nivel más bajo en 17 meses, ya que el descenso del rendimiento de los bonos gubernamentales franceses atenuaba los temores sobre la tensión en los mercados de deuda de la zona euro. * La moneda única ganaba un 0,28% , a 1,1252 dólares, encaminándose a su mayor subida diaria desde el 3 de septiembre. El lunes tocó su mínimo desde mayo de 2025, a 1,116 dólares, tras un declive superior al 1% la semana pasada, su cuarto descenso semanal consecutivo. * El índice dólar , que compara al billete verde con una cesta de seis destacadas monedas, restaba un 0,26%, a 101,89 unidades, en camino a su mayor caída diaria desde el 25 de septiembre. * Los mercados mundiales de bonos han registrado un aumento de los rendimientos por las expectativas de fuertes alzas de las tasas de interés, tras el repunte de los precios de la energía a raíz de la guerra en Irán, así como la preocupación sobre las finanzas públicas. * La deuda francesa se ha visto sometida a una presión cada vez mayor, mientras los políticos luchan por limitar el déficit presupuestario de cara a las divisivas elecciones de 2027. La convocatoria de elecciones anticipadas en España se sumaba a la presión reciente sobre el euro. * Los precios del crudo bajaban, ya que el aumento de las exportaciones de crudo de Oriente Medio y la liberación de reservas de emergencia del G7 aliviaban las preocupaciones sobre el suministro. * Asimismo, las fuerzas gubernamentales yemeníes respaldadas por Arabia Saudita llevaron a cabo el lunes un avance relámpago para recuperar la costa alrededor del estrecho de Bab el-Mandeb hasta la ciudad de Mocha, según informó el Gobierno. * La libra esterlina subía un 0,39%, a 1,327 dólares. Frente al yen, la moneda estadounidense avanzaba un 0,05%, a 157,98 unidades.

FAST

BENGALURU, Oct 6 : Kenny Bednarek says he is gunning for gold at next year's world championships in Beijing and the Los Angeles Olympics in 2028 after shedding his "silver man" tag with a sprint double at the World Athletics Ultimate Championship last month. The American has been a perennial contender over 200 metres, winning two Olympic and two world championships silver medals, but his breakthrough sprint double in Budapest offered proof he is a threat over both distances on the big stage. Bednarek, 27, told Reuters in a video interview that his multiple runner-up finishes had left him wanting more. "It's one of the most important things to be somebody who's always there, but it's also a bittersweet situation because ... you're clearly one of the best but not the best," he said.

"That was the thing I wanted to improve on going into this year, hit a lot of good times and get some wins here and there. My goal was to make sure to put everything together when it mattered the most. "Finally getting global championships, gold medals, it was a sigh of relief. You've probably heard people call me the 'silver man' and all that. So it was getting that stigma off of me and proving myself right." The headband-wearing American, nicknamed "Kung Fu Kenny", finished seventh in the Paris Olympics 100m final but said the work he has been doing to improve his start has been paying off. With sprint king Usain Bolt watching from the stands in Budapest, Bednarek clocked 9.85 seconds to beat Jamaican world champion Oblique Seville. "My Achilles heel has always been my reaction time and sometimes maybe just not getting out of the blocks the way I wanted to," said Bednarek, who posted a personal best of 9.79 seconds in the 100m last year. "When we were going into this year, it was about being consistent and more intentional with what I was doing coming out of the blocks, not trying to sit in when the gun goes off." 'CHANGE MY LIFE' Winning the 200m in Budapest over a field that included 2020 Olympic champion Andre De Grasse and Paris Games gold medallist Letsile Tebogo was a huge confidence booster, he said. "Winning the 100m and 200m, especially in the fashion I did doing four races in two days, that made my confidence go through the roof," he added. "It's something I've been trying to do over the last few years and I was finally able to. Knowing exactly what I did, the preparation and work I put in leading up to the races gives me a blueprint of what I need to do in the future. "I'm very confident doing the same thing, going to the world championships and the Olympics." Bednarek looked forward to competing at an Olympics on home soil in 2028 and said winning gold would be life changing. "I think it plays a little bit of a role ... it's in Los Angeles, so all my family members will definitely be able to go," he added. "It definitely adds a lot more motivation, being able to win a gold or more than one. The whole of the US will be watching. I think it also would be a bit easier just because we don't have to travel and deal with jet lag. "I think winning those gold medals will change my life and other people's lives. A lot more opportunities would be open. We'll see what happens."

Source: Reuters

item.title: Emmy Awards to leave broadcast TV for Amazon's Prime Video in 2027
item.description: The Television Academy and Amazon's Prime Video on Tuesday announced a six-year deal making the streaming service the exclusive global home of the Emmys, ending the awards show's rotation among US broadcast networks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Television Academy and Amazon's Prime Video (AMZN.O) on Tuesday announced a six-year deal making the streaming service the exclusive global home of the Emmys, ending the awards show's rotation among US broadcast networks. The deal will take effect with the 2027 ceremony and ends the traditional "Wheel Deal" rotation under which the telecast alternated among broadcast networks ABC, CBS, Fox and NBC, concluding with this year's show. Traditional television networks face growing competition from streaming services, which have increasingly taken on major live events and awards shows as viewing habits shift toward digital platforms. [USN:L4N3XN1KE TEXT:"Organizers"] of the annual Academy Awards said last year that the Oscar telecast was moving from the ABC broadcast network to stream live on YouTube around the world starting 2029. The Emmy Awards ceremony will continue to air live in September but will be available free to viewers worldwide, with no Prime Video subscription required, Amazon said. The financial terms of the deal were not disclosed. For Prime Video, the agreement adds another high-profile live entertainment property to a service that has expanded through original films and television shows, sports and other streaming partnerships. The Emmys, first held in 1949, honor achievements in television acting, production and writing, among other areas. The awards have traditionally served as a major promotional and cultural event for the US television industry.

item.title: IEA to decide on details of diesel stocks release next week, sources say, as market confusion grows
item.description: The West's energy watchdog will meet next week to work out the details of a diesel stock release as market confusion grows over how many barrels Europe and the US plan to make available to address shortages and record-high prices, sources said.
item.dc:creator: Giuseppe Fonte, Kate Abnett, Alex Lawler
item.content:encoded: The West's energy watchdog will meet next week to work out the details of a diesel stock release as market confusion grows over how many barrels Europe and the US plan to make available to address shortages and record-high prices, sources said. The surge in diesel prices has turned the fuel, which underpins trucking, agriculture and industry, into a global political and economic concern. The wars in Iran and Ukraine have curtailed exports and damaged refineries, helping drive the rise in prices. Under pressure from US President Donald Trump, the Group of Seven major economies agreed on Friday to release [USN:L6N45O0G5 TEXT:"100 million barrels"] of diesel and crude oil from emergency reserves and pledged to refrain from energy export restrictions. They did not provide a breakdown of the volumes of crude, diesel and other products to be released, however, or say which countries would participate. The governing board of the International Energy Agency, which advises industrialised countries and manages their strategic oil reserves, is expected to decide the details of the stocks release at an October 14-15 board meeting, two people close to the matter said on Tuesday. The Paris-based IEA did not immediately respond to a request for comment on what was expected to be decided at the board meeting. The G7 includes the US, UK, Japan and Canada along with EU nations France, Germany and Italy. DETAILS ON NEW RELEASE UNCLEAR G7 member Italy would be part of the release, one of the sources said. The EU's oil coordination group will meet on Wednesday, a European Commission spokesperson said on Tuesday. The White House did not immediately respond to a request to clarify details of the stocks release. The Iran war sparked the biggest emergency stock release ever of 400 million barrels in March, which was coordinated by the IEA. Announcing the new stocks release, G7 leaders said last Friday they would take into account commitments already fulfilled regarding the previous move. Oil market participants and some EU government officials were trying on Tuesday to work out the finer points of the Friday announcement. Russell Hardy, chief executive of Vitol, said at a conference in London on Tuesday that the commodities trading house was still trying to understand the details of the stocks release. "It wasn't a fully transparent announcement about exactly what was being released where," he said. "And so over the next two weeks, we'll see tenders coming out from different bodies, and those tenders will tell us exactly how much oil and in which location it's going to come out."

item.title: Polícia lança gás lacrimogêneo contra manifestantes no dia de maior mobilização estudantil na França
item.description: A polícia lançou gás lacrimogêneo contra manifestantes que bloqueavam escolas de ensino médio francesas nesta terça-feira, enquanto alunos, professores e pais saíram às ruas no maior dia de mobilização de uma onda de manifestações contra salas de aula com falta de pessoal e em estado de degradação.
item.dc:creator: Tilman Blasshofer, Cecile Mantovani, Lucien Libert
item.content:encoded: A polícia lançou gás lacrimogêneo contra manifestantes que bloqueavam escolas de ensino médio francesas nesta terça-feira, enquanto alunos, professores e pais saíram às ruas no maior dia de mobilização de uma onda de manifestações contra salas de aula com falta de pessoal e em estado de degradação. Em Marselha e Nantes, os manifestantes exibiram cartazes com frases como “O Estado matou a educação nacional” e outras mensagens, em manifestações em grande parte pacíficas. Em Toulouse, os pais deram as mãos na frente de uma marcha pela cidade. Mas em Estrasburgo, Lyon e Rennes, as manifestações chegaram a se tornar violentas em alguns momentos, com a polícia lançando gás lacrimogêneo e os manifestantes acendendo fogueiras nas ruas e atirando objetos. “Existe uma enorme distância entre as elites e nós”, disse Hugo Vetzel, recém-formado no ensino médio em Estrasburgo. Os protestos começaram em setembro nos subúrbios carentes de Paris, antes de se espalharem por todo o país, representando um grande desafio para o governo do presidente Emmanuel Macron, que enfrenta dificuldades financeiras em um momento em que o país enfrenta fortes dificuldades econômicas. A União dos Estudantes do Ensino Médio informou que mais da metade das escolas de ensino médio da França estavam bloqueadas ou fechariam durante o dia. Algumas autoridades educacionais locais tentaram transferir as aulas para o ambiente virtual. “Queremos mais recursos para o sistema educacional nacional, para que as escolas de ensino médio sejam reformadas”, disse Roberta, outra recém-formada do ensino médio, em um protesto em frente à prestigiada escola Henri IV, em Paris. As escolas enfrentavam uma série de problemas, desde vazamentos de água até infestações de ratos, acrescentou ela. MILHARES DE PRISÕES O governo respondeu às manifestações com a polícia de choque. Grupos de direitos humanos, estudantes e associações de pais acusaram as autoridades de usar força desproporcional contra menores. O governo afirma que o movimento de protesto foi sequestrado por pessoas de fora e se transformou em violência urbana. O Ministério do Interior da França informou que 6.100 pessoas foram presas desde o início dos protestos, sendo a esmagadora maioria delas menores de idade. Mais de 1.800 pessoas estão sendo processadas, incluindo 1.483 menores, informou o Ministério da Justiça, sem especificar os crimes. Pelo menos 715 policiais e 215 adolescentes ficaram feridos nos confrontos, segundo o gabinete do primeiro-ministro da França, Sébastien Lecornu. A mão de um adolescente foi arrancada durante confrontos entre manifestantes do ensino médio e a polícia de choque no norte da França na segunda-feira. O jornal regional La Voix du Nord informou que o jovem de 15 anos perdeu a mão e parte do antebraço após pegar uma granada de dispersão da polícia. “Eles querem dividir os jovens em manifestantes bons e maus”, disse Omar Slaouti, professor do ensino médio em Argenteuil, um subúrbio a noroeste de Paris. “Se não houvesse lixeiras em chamas, o governo não teria recuado e tomado consciência das questões em jogo”, acrescentou ele. Seis meses antes da eleição para substituir Macron, seu governo e o partido de extrema direita Reunião Nacional (RN), da candidata à Presidência Marine de Le Pen, acusaram deputados e prefeitos da extrema esquerda do partido França Insubmissa (LFI) de incitar os protestos. O LFI nega a acusação. LECORNU PROMETE RESPOSTA Lecornu ordenou que seus ministros atendam às principais reivindicações dos estudantes. Entre elas estão garantir a substituição de professores ausentes, rever a duração do dia letivo, que vai das 8h às 18h, e a necessidade de intervalos mais longos para o almoço. O governo também analisará os reparos necessários nos prédios escolares antigos, disse Lecornu, que exigiu que os ministros apresentassem suas primeiras propostas até o final de outubro. A mãe Emilie Lhomme disse, durante um protesto em frente à escola Helene Boucher, em Paris, que as palavras do governo não são suficientes. “Tudo isso é muito bom, mas não é isso que vai mudar o dia a dia dos nossos filhos”, afirmou ela. Encontrar recursos financeiros para implementar as reformas educacionais será difícil. O governo está sob pressão para tentar reduzir um déficit orçamentário que cresce vertiginosamente, à medida que as preocupações dos investidores com o aumento da dívida da França, o fraco crescimento e a relutância em conter os gastos elevam os rendimentos dos títulos. O rendimento dos títulos franceses de 10 anos atingiu brevemente, na semana passada, a maior alta em 24 anos, ultrapassando 5%. O aumento nos custos de financiamento da França começou a se espalhar para toda a zona do euro, com a desvalorização do euro servindo como o mais recente sinal de alarme. O ministro das Finanças, Roland Lescure, afirmou na terça-feira que não havia necessidade de intervenção do Banco Central Europeu. Le Pen, a populista de extrema direita e eurocética que lidera a corrida presidencial antes das eleições do ano que vem, apresentou planos para cortar gastos públicos caso seja eleita, buscando estabelecer sua credibilidade fiscal à medida que a crise no mercado de títulos se agrava. (Reportagem de Tilman Blasshofer, em Estrasburgo; Cecile Mantovani, em Lyon; Lucien Libert e Juliette Jabkhiro, em Paris; Layli Foroudi, em Argenteuil, e Inti Landauro e Sudip Kar-Gupta, em Bruxelas)

item.title: German bank board member to leave despite clean brothel loan probe
item.description: A board member of Germany's Volksbank Koeln Bonn will leave the lender despite a law firm commissioned by the bank finding no wrongdoing in connection with financing for one of Europe's largest brothels, the bank said on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Tom Sims
item.content:encoded: A board member of Germany's Volksbank Koeln Bonn will leave the lender despite a law firm commissioned by the bank finding no wrongdoing in connection with financing for one of Europe's largest brothels, the bank said on Tuesday. The co-operative bank placed board member [USN:L6N44N08S TEXT:"Juergen Neutgens"] on leave over the summer and hired the law firm to review a pandemic-era loan used to finance Cologne's Pascha brothel. The bank said on Tuesday the investigation had found "no evidence of financial irregularities or misconduct in the lending transactions and business relationships" examined. "However ... the necessary basis for a relationship of trust and impartial cooperation can no longer be maintained going forward," it added. Neutgens has previously denied wrongdoing through his lawyer, who confirmed to Reuters on Tuesday the mutual agreement to part ways despite the report clearing Neutgens of any wrongdoing. The case centres on a €5 million ($5.6 million) loan granted in 2021 to fund the purchase of a 12-storey property by a Chinese investor after the brothel within it went insolvent during COVID lockdowns, according to corporate filings, property records and people familiar with the matter. Prostitution is legal in Germany, but the law firm's investigation examined whether Neutgens had "possibly personally benefited" from the transaction, Volksbank has previously said. As Reuters [USN:L6N44N08S TEXT:"reported"] in August, Cologne prosecutors opened a separate investigation into Neutgens and two other bank employees on suspicion of bribery, according to a person with direct knowledge of the matter. Prosecutors said on Tuesday their investigation was ongoing and that they had requested a copy of the bank's independent investigation to examine for themselves. Neutgens' lawyer said he expected prosecutors to eventually exonerate his client. Germany's financial regulator BaFin has also questioned the bank over the brothel financing, [USN:L8N44M0EZ TEXT:"Reuters has reported"]. Germany's Volksbanken are member-owned cooperative banks that form a key pillar of the country's banking sector. They rarely lend to foreign borrowers abroad and generally avoid business that could damage their reputation. ($1 = €0.8879)

item.title: 北朝鮮、地雷爆発巡る韓国正式見解に反発 「重大な挑発」
item.description:
Kyu-seok Shim
［ソウル ６日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Kyu-seok Shim

［ソウル　６日　ロイター］ - 北朝鮮外務省は６日、南北境界地域の非武装地帯（ＤＭＺ）で韓国軍兵士２人が重傷を負った地雷爆発を巡る韓国の非難を一蹴し、領土を侵犯すれば「即時かつ強力な対抗措置」を取ると警告した。国営朝鮮中央通信（ＫＣＮＡ）が伝えた。

韓国軍は５日、ＤＭＺでの爆発は、北朝鮮が仕掛けた地雷によるものだと結論付ける調査結果を発表した。

北朝鮮外務省は、韓国軍の発表は、爆発を北朝鮮と結び付けて北朝鮮への外交・軍事的措置を正当化するための「計画的な茶番劇」だと指摘。調査結果は「重大な挑発」で北朝鮮の主権を侵害するものだと非難した。

「韓国の軍靴や火花がほんの１ミリでも国境を越えてわが領土を侵犯すれば、北朝鮮の国境警備部隊は即時かつ強力な対抗措置を取る」とした。

さらに、韓国が進める地雷除去作業には関知しないとし、韓国側で同様の事案が再び起きた場合、責任は全て韓国にあると警告した。

韓国国防省の報道官は６日、地雷爆発を巡り、北朝鮮に謝罪を迫る対応策を準備していると明らかにした。金正恩朝鮮労働党総書記の妹である金与正党総務部長は２日、韓国側の謝罪要求を退けている。

item.title: Paramount wraps up mega Warner Bros merger to create Hollywood powerhouse Skydance
item.description: Paramount Skydance on Tuesday completed its blockbuster $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery , creating a Hollywood heavyweight called Skydance and handing CEO David Ellison control of one of the world's largest entertainment companies.
item.dc:creator: Anzar Mehraj, Harshita Varghese
item.content:encoded: Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) on Tuesday completed its blockbuster $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery (WBD.O) , creating a Hollywood heavyweight called Skydance and handing CEO David Ellison control of one of the world's largest entertainment companies. The deal brings together the studios behind "Mission: Impossible," "Harry Potter" and DC Studios alongside major television and streaming networks such as CBS, CNN, Paramount+ and HBO Max — forming an expansive entertainment company spanning film, TV and news. Shares of the combined company moved to the New York Stock Exchange from Nasdaq on Tuesday to trade under the ticker "SKYD." [USN:L4N45D11C TEXT:"Settlements"] with a coalition of US states and a Hollywood writers union removed the main legal barriers to the merger, one of the largest in media history. It comes as Hollywood faces declining cable-TV subscriptions, high cost of competing for streaming audiences and persistent pressure from unions over jobs and creative workers' rights. Ellison [USN:L6N45O0RY TEXT:"said last week"] the Skydance name was chosen to retain the individual identities of Paramount and Warner Bros studios, rather than combining them under a new brand. Analysts, however, said the name reinforces the extent of Ellison's control, highlighting how some of Hollywood's most iconic brands now answer to him and how he has a platform to impose his strategy and culture. In just 16 years, Skydance has gone from an independent studio to the center of one of Hollywood's biggest power plays. Founded in 2010 by the son of Oracle co-founder Larry Ellison, it built its reputation as a financial backer and producer of Paramount's blockbuster "Top Gun: Maverick." After [USN:L4N3TZ1NM TEXT:"merging with"] Paramount last year, Skydance set its sights on Warner Bros, entering a heated bidding contest with Netflix (NFLX.O) while drawing interest from other potential suitors, including Comcast (CMCSA.O) . Warner Bros shareholders received an additional $41.9 million in "ticking fee," based on the number of days between September-end and the deal-closing, according to a regulatory filing. BROADER HOLLYWOOD BET Ellison named Mattel's former CEO Ynon Kreiz as Skydance co-CEO to run day-to-day operations and lead the integration, while Ellison oversees creative direction and overall strategy. The duo faces the task of combining two large companies while delivering $6 billion in planned cost savings, a big part of which Paramount said would come from "non-labor sources" — by combining streaming technologies and cloud providers of the two companies. However, the scale of the cuts is expected to affect jobs across Hollywood. Skydance plans to combine its streaming services, including HBO Max and Paramount+, into a single service and has [USN:L1N45D0VR TEXT:"pledged to release at least 30 films"] each in the first two years after closing, rising to 32 a year for the following three. The combined company is also expected to carry about $80 billion in debt, putting pressure on Ellison to grow streaming, preserve cash flow from cable networks and improve theatrical film performance. Analysts at MoffettNathanson forecast EBITDA of $16 billion for 2028, rising to $19 billion in 2030. The brokerage also predicted about $67 billion in revenue in 2028 for the company, growing to roughly $70 billion in 2030. CNN chief Mark Thompson and CBS News Editor-in-Chief Bari Weiss [USN:L6N45R0R0 TEXT:"will continue"] in their respective leadership roles. Ellison's annual base salary will be $5 million, with a target annual bonus of $5 million, according to the filing.

ROME, Oct 6 : Italy's soccer federation president Giovanni Malago is set to lose his job and return as a special administrator under a compromise crafted by the Italian Olympic Committee (CONI) on Tuesday which ends weeks of governance upheaval. The Olympic body's executive board voted unanimously to place the Italian Football Federation (FIGC) under extraordinary administration and propose Malago to oversee daily operations, subject to final ratification by its National Council. The move offers a political exit route following weeks of administrative friction after Malago won the federation presidency in June with over 68 per cent of the vote. Legal inquiries commissioned by the Olympic authorities had questioned the validity of the ballot over technical non-compliance because Malago was not a member of the FIGC at the time of his election.

Malago will be eligible to stand as a candidate in the election that is to be held no later than January 31 next year.  The leadership dispute comes at a critical moment for Italian football, which faces pressing structural challenges, including venue upgrades required to co-host Euro 2032 and the sporting fallout from missing three consecutive World Cups.

item.title: ArriVent's cancer pill fails to 'meaningfully' delay disease progression, shares dive
item.description: ArriVent BioPharma said on Tuesday its oral therapy to treat patients with a rare type of lung cancer did not significantly delay disease progression in a late-stage trial, sending its shares plunging nearly 60% in morning trading.
item.dc:creator: Christy Santhosh
item.content:encoded: ArriVent BioPharma (AVBP.O) said on Tuesday its oral therapy to treat patients with a rare type of lung cancer did not significantly delay disease progression in a late-stage trial, sending its shares plunging nearly 60% in morning trading. The therapy, firmonertinib, was tested in previously untreated patients with advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and a genetic alteration called EGFR exon 20 insertion mutation, which can fuel cancer growth. The mutation occurs in roughly 0.5% to 1% of all NSCLC cases. NSCLC accounts for about 85% of all lung cancer cases. In the trial, a 240-milligram dose of ArriVent's therapy extended median progression-free survival to 11 months versus 9.5 months with chemotherapy, an assessment by independent reviewers showed. CEO Bing Yao said the improvement in progression-free survival - a measure of time patients lived without the disease worsening or spreading - was not "meaningful." "These disappointing results are not what we hoped for, particularly for the patients ... who urgently need more effective treatment options." The company said it was evaluating the full dataset to determine the most appropriate development path for firmonertinib and that no new safety signals were identified in the trial. The trial appears to have failed mainly because the control arm outperformed expectations, delivering 9.5 months of progression-free survival versus the estimated 7.5 to 8 months, while firmonertinib's 11 months was in line with the expected 9 to 11 months, said BTIG analyst Jeet Mukherjee. Firmonertinib is also being tested in a late-stage trial for patients with NSCLC whose tumors contain uncommon EGFR PACC mutations. "The result is a meaningful setback for the exon20 opportunity, however, the PACC program has clinical support," said Clear Street analyst Kaveri Pohlman. The therapy is approved in China for NSCLC patients with certain mutations.

item.title: McKesson, CD&R to take infusion therapy provider Option Care private in $5.8 billion deal
item.description: Drug distributor McKesson and private equity firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice on Tuesday agreed to take infusion therapy provider Option Care Health private in a deal worth about $5.8 billion including debt.
item.dc:creator: Sneha K
item.content:encoded: Drug distributor McKesson (MCK.N) and private equity firm Clayton Dubilier & Rice on Tuesday agreed to take infusion therapy provider Option Care Health (OPCH.O) private in a deal worth about $5.8 billion including debt. The per-share offer price of $32.05 represents a 37.1% premium to Option Care's last closing price. Its shares were up 32.8% at $31.03. The deal is the latest for the US drug distributor as it seeks to expand its healthcare services footprint, and marks another private equity buyout of a home health services provider after [USN:L4N3ZJ0UX TEXT:"Enhabit"]. Option Care Health is the largest independent infusion therapy provider in the US, serving more than 308,000 patients annually through over 197 locations to provide services such as home and ambulatory infusions, specialty pharmacy and care for complex conditions. McKesson's focus on specialty and the community setting makes this deal appealing, allowing it to leverage supply chain efficiencies and work with Option Care Health in complex chronic drugs, said J.P.Morgan analyst Lisa Gill. There has been growing demand for home‑based care in the US, as the population ages and more patients choose to receive treatment outside higher-cost settings like hospitals. According to the terms of the deal, McKesson will invest about $1.4 billion for a 49% minority interest, holding the right to purchase the remaining 51% from CD&R at some point in the future. Option Care Health will remain a separate company led by its own management team. The transaction aligns McKesson with the site-of-care shift away from hospital and provider settings, said Leerink Partners analyst Michael Cherny in a note late on Monday. The deal would also expand McKesson's US footprint in home infusion services as it currently operates Inviva, a leading infusion network in Canada. McKesson's oncology and multispecialty segment that includes infusion services recorded revenue of $14.2 billion in the latest quarter, a rise of 33% from a year earlier. The deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027, and Option Care Health will become a privately held company.

FAST

The United States has discussed starting reciprocal visits to nuclear sites with China, and plans to continue pushing in meetings in the coming months, CNN reported on Tuesday (Oct 6), citing sources familiar with the matter.

The idea of reciprocal visits was initially raised by China in meetings with US officials this year and visits to US Department of Energy national laboratories and equivalent Chinese facilities were discussed, CNN said, citing a source.

The discussions between US and Chinese officials have mainly been on the sidelines of gatherings by the UN Security Council's five veto-wielding permanent members, CNN reported.

Reuters could not immediately verify the report. The White House and the Chinese embassy in Washington did not respond to requests for comment outside business hours.

US President Donald Trump called for trilateral arms control negotiations between the US, China and Russia when he met President Xi Jinping last month. However, the two leaders did not discuss the possibility of nuclear site visits during their talks, the CNN report said, citing a US official.

Beijing has said its nuclear arsenal is far smaller than those of Russia and the US, something it says makes its participation in such talks unnecessary.

Another meeting between Trump and Xi is widely considered likely this year, potentially at November's Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China or during Group of 20 meetings in the US in December.

By the time the two leaders meet again, it is expected that further lower-level discussions on possible nuclear site visits will have taken place, CNN said.

item.title: Energy Transfer to buy Vaquero Midstream for $2.63 billion in cash-and-stock deal
item.description: Energy Transfer said on Tuesday it has agreed to acquire Vaquero Midstream in a deal valued at about $2.6 billion in cash and stock, expanding the pipeline company's midstream operations.
item.dc:creator: Pranav Mathur
item.content:encoded: Energy Transfer said on Tuesday it has agreed to acquire Vaquero Midstream in a deal valued at about $2.6 billion in cash and stock, expanding the pipeline company's midstream operations. The deal includes $1.95 billion in cash and about 33.3 million of its newly issued shares, Energy Transfer said. It [USN:L6N3Y70P9 TEXT:"expects to invest"] between $5 billion and $5.5 billion in capital in 2026, primarily in its natural gas network projects, the company said earlier this year. Shares of Energy Transfer fell 1.2% in morning trading. It said the assets, which are linked to its existing natural gas and natural gas liquids infrastructure, would provide additional volumes for its transportation, fractionation, terminalling and export businesses. "This is a continuation of midstream consolidation as the sector rolls up, highlighting the value of the assets," said James West, an analyst at Melius Research. He said the combination of inorganic and organic expansion projects was positioning midstream companies for a decade-plus growth cycle and could support further upside valuation across the sector. The acquisition is expected to close in the fourth quarter of the year. Vaquero operates roughly 300 miles of pipeline across the Loving, Reeves, Ward and Winkler counties in Texas, servicing producers in the Southern Delaware Basin. Its Caymus Processing Complex has three processing trains with a combined capacity of about 675 million cubic feet per day. Vaquero's contracts are fee-based and supported by about 100,000 dedicated acres, with an average remaining contract term of approximately 10 years.

item.title: Líder separatista catalão Puigdemont deve retornar à Espanha após tribunal revogar mandado de prisão
item.description: Os dois principais tribunais da Espanha abriram caminho, nesta terça-feira, para que o líder separatista catalão Carles Puigdemont, autoexilado, possa retornar sem ser preso, justamente quando a Espanha se prepara para eleições nacionais antecipadas.
item.dc:creator: Joan Faus, Emma Pinedo
item.content:encoded: Os dois principais tribunais da Espanha abriram caminho, nesta terça-feira, para que o líder separatista catalão Carles Puigdemont, autoexilado, possa retornar sem ser preso, justamente quando a Espanha se prepara para eleições nacionais antecipadas. O Tribunal Constitucional decidiu que uma lei de anistia para separatistas catalães se aplica às acusações de peculato contra Puigdemont. Pouco depois, o Supremo Tribunal respondeu revogando o mandado de prisão contra Puigdemont. O provável retorno do ex-chefe de governo catalão pode desestabilizar ainda mais um cenário político já volátil antes das eleições de 29 de novembro. Puigdemont fugiu para a Bélgica em 2017 após realizar um referendo de independência para sua região, que Madri havia declarado ilegal. “É uma grande vitória para o presidente Puigdemont e os outros dois líderes exilados” na Bélgica, disse Jordi Turull, secretário-geral do partido Junts, de Puigdemont, aos repórteres. “Eles se mantiveram firmes, resistiram, prevaleceram na Europa e hoje prevaleceram contra o Estado espanhol.” Ele se recusou a dizer quando Puigdemont poderia retornar, mas descartou a possibilidade de ele concorrer nas próximas eleições. O primeiro-ministro da Espanha, Pedro Sánchez, havia promulgado a anistia no âmbito de um acordo de 2023 entre seu Partido Socialista e dois partidos catalães, incluindo o Junts, de Puigdemont, em troca do apoio deles para que ele permanecesse como primeiro-ministro. A medida provocou intensa oposição social e política por parte dos críticos do governo na época. O Supremo Tribunal havia inicialmente decidido que a anistia não se aplicava ao crime de peculato, o que significava que Puigdemont e outros ainda poderiam ser presos sob a acusação de desviar os recursos gastos no referendo. Mas o Tribunal Constitucional, que conta com uma maioria de tendência progressista, decidiu, em recurso, que negar a anistia para o crime de desvio de verbas não relacionado ao enriquecimento pessoal violaria o objetivo da lei de anistia. “A decisão está em linha com as expectativas, pois sempre defendemos que a lei de anistia era constitucional e também compatível com a legislação da União Europeia”, disse o advogado de Puigdemont, Gonzalo Boye, à Reuters. Há um ano, o Junts retirou seu apoio ao governo central minoritário da Espanha. Incapaz de aprovar leis, Sánchez convocou eleições antecipadas na segunda-feira. Sánchez disse aos repórteres nesta terça-feira que não se arrependeu de ter lançado a anistia e acolheu com satisfação a decisão do tribunal. “Acredito que a mensagem importante seja a da coexistência entre os catalães”, disse ele. Embora o separatismo tenha perdido força e o Junts esteja atrás nas pesquisas de opinião, o retorno de Puigdemont pode desencadear um novo drama político. O Partido Popular, de direita, lidera as pesquisas de opinião antes das eleições e pode precisar buscar o apoio do Junts e de outros partidos de centro-direita para governar. A Catalunha declarou unilateralmente a independência da Espanha em 2017, após o referendo. Embora cerca de 90% dos eleitores tenham apoiado a independência, os catalães que queriam permanecer como parte da Espanha boicotaram em grande parte a votação, e muitas seções eleitorais foram fechadas. Puigdemont fugiu do país, enquanto vários de seus ex-ministros, incluindo Turull, permaneceram no país e foram presos, sendo posteriormente perdoados por Sánchez. (Reportagem de Joan Faus e Emma Pinedo)

item.title: ロシアのペスト研究所職員死亡、接触者に感染確認されず＝衛生当局
item.description: [モスクワ／シェレホフ（ロシア） ６日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[モスクワ／シェレホフ（ロシア）　６日　ロイター] - ロシアの衛生監視機関である消費者権利保護・福祉監督庁（ロスポトレブナゾール）は６日、２日に死亡したシベリアのペスト研究所職員と接触した人の間で、ペストの発症例は確認されていないと発表した。

ロシアでは、東シベリアのイルクーツク近郊にあるシベリア・極東ペスト対策研究所に勤めていた２８歳の女性研究員が原因不明の肺炎で死亡。この件を巡っては、トランプ米大統領を含む国際社会から懸念の声が上がっている。

ロスポトレブナゾールは声明で、同研究所の職員の間で過去１０日間に感染症の報告はなく、詳しい検査でも死亡した女性の体内から業務に関連する微生物は見つからなかったと発表。公衆衛生関連法に基づき包括的な防疫措置を直ちに実施し、患者と接触した可能性のある人を病院での医学観察下で検査を毎日実施した結果、接触者の中に感染症に関連する健康状態の変化がみられた者はいなかったと明らかにした。

イルクーツク近郊シェレホフ地区のソフィナ副地区長も、危険な感染症は確認されなかったと述べた。同地区では地元の病院が隔離措置の対象となっているが、隔離された人の約６０％はすでに解除されたという。

item.description: LONDON, Oct 6 : US start-up Type One Energy has raised $200 million from investors including the venture unit of Germany's Siemens Energy, as it vies to build the world's first commercial fusion reactor, its chief executive told Reuters.The Series-B round, which takes total funding to-date to more than $400 m

Fusion firm Type One in $200 million Siemens Energy-backed raise

FAST

LONDON, Oct 6 : US start-up Type One Energy has raised $200 million from investors including the venture unit of Germany's Siemens Energy, as it vies to build the world's first commercial fusion reactor, its chief executive told Reuters. The Series-B round, which takes total funding to-date to more than $400 million, is the third-biggest sector Series B raise over the last five years, data from industry tracker PitchBook showed. The company did not disclose its valuation. Fusion energy has been researched for decades. A wave of firms has launched in recent years as advances in magnets, computing and materials have fuelled hopes fusion technology could one day provide abundant clean power across the globe. Type One is backed by Bill Gates' Breakthrough Energy Ventures and Clutterbuck Capital. It is developing a stellarator, a type of fusion reactor that uses complex magnetic fields to contain superheated plasma, partnering with engineering, construction and other companies to speed up delivery and reduce costs.

Chief Executive Christofer Mowry said the funds would help further develop its technology, including the deployment of an engineering prototype machine, Infinity One. "It's not an experimental science project... the only thing that we want to learn is that our design for the fusion machine in the power plant works as advertised." Project Infinity is based at Bull Run in Tennessee and Type One hopes to launch the commercial plant, Infinity Two, within a decade. It aims to work towards a manufacturing partnership with Siemens. Enrique Gonzalez Zanetich, partner at Siemens Energy Ventures, said in a statement that the deal strengthened his company's position in fusion "as we continue to explore the technologies and collaborations that can help advance commercialization". New investors alongside Siemens included Lowercarbon Capital, co-founded by early Uber backer Chris Sacca, and SiteGround Capital.
